title: readpdb: single-atom residues
purpose: Exercises `readpdb` [@pdbformat,@epsrmanual] with residues of a single atom (ions), element names taken from columns 13-14 of the atom name with upper-case symbol matching (`NA`, `CL`), and a `HETATM` record, which `readpdb` ignores because only `ATOM` records are read.
fortran: `readpdb.f`: `run_readpdb`, `readpdb` (CRYST1/ATOM/CONECT records, molecules from residues, bonds from van der Waals radii, angle constraints, DIH groups), `upcase`
system: A hand-made aqueous NaCl fragment in a cubic 15 Å cell: three water molecules, one Na and one Cl residue (5 molecules, 11 atoms read; a `HETATM` carbon is skipped). Bonds are found where the distance is below 0.75 × the sum of the van der Waals radii; no dihedral groups.
inputs: `ions.pdb` written by hand; stdin `readpdb.stdin`: factor `0.75`, dihedrals `n`; `vanderWaalsRadii.txt` copied from EPSR-test.
verification: Output compared: `ions.ato`, in which the Na and Cl molecules appear with `nato = 1` but no atom records and their centres at the origin, exactly as written by the Fortran. Fortran reference: the original `readxyz`/`readpdb` binaries crash (SIGSEGV) at the first call of `ctype`, which has optional arguments but is called with 11 of its 13 arguments without an explicit interface (gfortran passes the hidden character lengths where `radmaxsph`/`pseudofacsph` are expected). The reference was therefore produced with an explicit `INTERFACE` block for `ctype` added to the program (no other change; absent arguments mean `radmaxsphere = 0.5*sigcor`, `pseudofacmol = 1`), built by `rust/tools/build_patched_readxyz_readpdb.sh`; the comparison is against this patched build, not the original binary.
notes: Fortran quirk reproduced: for a one-atom residue `nal` is never set (it is assigned only when a second atom is added) and keeps 0, so the loops `naf..nal` are empty and the ions are effectively lost.
